_comment: Memorise behaviour knobs. The books are in lib/memorise/books.js and the rules that use these numbers are in lib/memorise/memorise.js; this file is only what those numbers are, so changing how much a page holds or how many words a gap offers is an edit here and nowhere else.
_comment-page: About how many words a page holds before the next line starts a new one. Sized from the 15-line Madani mushaf, which is the script this app already renders, so a page here holds about what one of its pages holds: 15 lines of roughly nine words. A book whose lines are not ayah-shaped sets its own wordsPerPage in books.js.
_comment-options: How many words a gap offers when the reader is picking rather than typing is not here: it is the same question the quiz asks, so the number is kept once, as option-count in quiz.json, and this tab reads it from there. The control that turns picking on says the number out loud, so it is read and never typed into a label.
_comment-spacing: Two gaps never sit side by side while less than this share of a line is missing, because a run of blanks is one hard gap rather than two fair ones. From this share up there is no room left to keep that promise, so the rule steps aside rather than quietly hiding fewer words than asked. Raising it past a half would do exactly that.
_card-lead-in-s: How long before a word's own second in the recording "Mine" starts playing, so the word is heard whole and not from its middle.
_card-edge-px: The least gap kept between a word card and the edge of the screen when it hangs under a word near the side of the page.
_card-width-px: The width of a word card or an ayah card on a wide screen. On a phone it spans the screen and this is not used.
_card-phone-height-share: The most of the screen's height a word card may take on a phone, as a share. Past it the card's body scrolls and its buttons stay put, so the page and the live marks behind it stay in view.
_card-scroll-gap-px: On a phone, how far above the card the page is scrolled so the tapped word or ayah number sits just clear of it.
_turn-after-s: How long a finished page stays up before the next one turns in by itself, while reciting carries on. The page is finished once its last word is reached and the reciter has paused, and every sureness check of it is back; this is then only the moment to see how its last ayah went. Long enough to catch a red word, short enough that the new page is up before the reciter is far into it (the words said meanwhile are kept either way).
_comment-difficulties: How much is taken out, as one word in every N. Named rather than numbered because 'one word in four' is what a reader chooses; 0.25 is not. 'none' sits at the front rather than after 'all', because it is where a page is first opened to be read, not the far end of a difficulty ladder. The default must be one of these ids.

difficulties.title: Nothing is missing: the whole page, to read

difficulties.title: One word in every five is missing
